gaps.sentence: He was made ___ for the damage to the rental car.
gaps.explanation: In the passive, 'be made to do' takes the to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: He apologized for ___ so abrupt in the meeting.
He apologised for ___ so rude to the waiter.
gaps.explanation: 'Apologise for being' — 'for' is a preposition, so the gerund follows.
can't stand + -ing (also to-infinitive in AmE): can't stand waiting. -ing accepted as standard.

gaps.sentence: This new timetable will mean ___ earlier trains.
I'd rather you ___ smoke in here.
gaps.explanation: would rather + somebody + past simple: I'd rather you didn't smoke.

gaps.sentence: We can't risk ___ the deadline again.
I tried ___ the shelf up, but it was too heavy.
gaps.explanation: try + to-infinitive = attempt, make an effort.
